STRATEGY: Parent is a forgiving TFT-like policy that starts C, retaliates when opponent defects more than a threshold, forgives rare defections, and exploits near the endgame. The trace simulates the parent against the listed population opponents (always-defect, slot 5, slot 0, slot 1) and identifies weaknesses such as delayed retaliation against always-defect and a long conflict with slot 1. It proposes embedding opponent models or pattern detection to improve cumulative score.

STRATEGY: Parent is a forgiving TFT-like strategy that cooperates, forgives rare defections, and retaliates after repeated defections. The trace simulates it against slot1 (an exploiter that defects when opponent cooperation rate ≥85% and n≥20), finding a long costly conflict. It proposes revisions: retaliate immediately/firmly, punish longer, and occasionally defect early to keep cooperation rate below exploiter thresholds.

The trace simulates periodic defection and adaptive probing against slot 1, slot 5, and TFT-like opponents. It changes toward defecting every 5th round or probing when cooperation rate is high, to avoid exploitation thresholds and prevent probes.

STRATEGY: Parent cooperates by default, retaliates on defection, forgives based on opp_def <= n//10, and defects in endgame. Simulated against slot1, always-defect, and forgiving opponents. Changed to retaliate immediately, forgive only after cooperating, add periodic probing every 6th round, and defect more in endgame.
